weekly_synthesis.text: This week, the AI sector navigated a dual focus on core technical advancements and the practicalities of business operations. On the technical front, the field saw developments across AI models and data tooling,

briefing_top_n.title: You Can't Tell If I'm Real Anymore. And That's Now YouTube's Problem Too.
briefing_top_n.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefing_top_n.tldr: AI voice cloning is now sophisticated enough to fool viewers who aren't paying close attention, raising questions about accountability for synthetic content. While AI excels at polish, subtle human details remain difficult to replicate perfectly. Creators and companies will succeed by maintaining transparency, clearly disclosing AI use, and ensuring human oversight for all published content.

briefing_top_n.title: Quoting Sean Lynch
briefing_top_n.tldr: Sean Lynch commented on Hacker News that the key advantage of MCP (Multi-modal Conversational Processing) is its ability to handle authentication separately from the agent's context window, possibly even outside the harness. He suggests that an ideal MCP could function solely as an API authentication gateway, which would still be a significant achievement. The digest also notes recent articles on hosting HTML apps within Datasette, the capabilities of GLM-5.2 as a text-only LLM, and publishing WASM wheels to PyPI.

briefing_top_n.title: Premium: The Silicon Valley Bubble (Part 2)
briefing_top_n.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
briefing_top_n.tldr: Ed Zitron's "The Silicon Valley Bubble (Part 2)" argues that the AI industry, exemplified by OpenAI's significant financial losses, represents a "pseudo-cult" prioritizing venture capital over reality. The article criticizes the industry's reliance on hype and speculative promises, suggesting it has lost its pragmatic roots and is now driven by a desire to maintain an illusion of growth and capital flow. Zitron contends that this bubble distorts incentives and reshapes the tech industry, leading to reckless exuberance and a failure to create genuine value.

briefing_top_n.title: Your AI Skills Are Trapped | Here's How to Own Them
briefing_top_n.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefing_top_n.tldr: AI agent skills are currently trapped within specific tools like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, creating a significant problem for users who switch between platforms. This "procedural debt" means users must re-explain their work each time, hindering productivity. The author introduces "Open Skills" as a solution, aiming to make agent procedures portable and ownable, allowing users to build and compound their work across different AI tools.

briefing_top_n.title: Datasette Apps: Host custom HTML applications inside Datasette
briefing_top_n.tldr: Datasette has launched a new plugin called datasette-apps, which allows users to host custom HTML and JavaScript applications directly within Datasette. These applications run in a sandboxed iframe with strict security policies, enabling them to execute read-only SQL queries and, with configuration, write operations via stored queries. This feature aims to enhance Datasette's utility by enabling the creation of custom interfaces and visualizations for data exploration, with potential for LLM-assisted development.

cards.title: The first big exit in AI
cards.tldr: SpaceX is acquiring AI coding assistant Cursor for $60 billion in an all-stock deal, marking a significant exit in the AI space. Cursor also announced new features at its first conference, including a GitHub alternative called Origin and advancements in transitioning between local and cloud AI agents. Additionally, OpenAI's leaked financials suggest substantial revenue and costs for 2025, and Noam Shazeer, a key figure in AI research, is joining the company.

cards.title: Don't build more AI agents until you watch this
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The key to successful AI agents in 2026 will be maintenance, not just building them. Vercel notably improved its AI agent by removing most of its tools, highlighting that the real challenge lies in managing the agent's environment as models and data evolve. An unmaintained agent may not fail obviously but can operate on outdated information, leading to significant costs.

cards.title: Bye bye Fable
cards.tldr: Anthropic has discontinued its Fable 5 model, which was based on the Mythos architecture, just three days after its launch. This decision came after the US government reportedly raised concerns about a jailbreak vulnerability found in Fable, which Anthropic stated could also be exploited in other models like GPT-5.5. The government's reaction led to the suspension of access for foreign nationals, prompting Anthropic to disable the model entirely.

cards.title: Exclusive: OpenAI Losses Increased Nearly 8X in 2025, With Spending Hitting $34 Billion
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: OpenAI incurred significant financial losses in 2025, reporting a net loss attributable to the company of $38.5 billion on $13.07 billion in revenue, with total costs and expenses reaching $34 billion. This marks a substantial increase from 2024, when the company lost $5.09 billion. The company paid Microsoft $17.2 billion for services, primarily for research and development, while receiving $303 million from Microsoft and $867 million from SoftBank.

cards.title: AI's Brokenomics
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: Anthropic faced US export controls on its Mythos and Fable AI models due to national security concerns, with reports suggesting potential access by China and a dispute over the severity of security breaches. This event highlights the precarious economics of AI, as both Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly considering drastic price cuts for their token-based services. The author argues that the "tokenomics bubble" is bursting because customers are realizing the high costs and lack of clear ROI, suggesting that the business models of major AI labs are unsustainable and dependent on massive subsidies from hyperscalers.

He suggests that an ideal MCP could function solely as an API authentication gateway, which would still be a significant achievement. The digest also notes recent articles on hosting HTML apps within Datasette, the capabilities of GLM-5.2 as a text-only LLM, and publishing WASM wheels to PyPI.

cards.title: Datasette Apps: Host custom HTML applications inside Datasette
cards.tldr: Datasette has launched a new plugin called datasette-apps, which allows users to host custom HTML and JavaScript applications directly within Datasette. These applications run in a sandboxed iframe with strict security policies, enabling them to execute read-only SQL queries and, with configuration, write operations via stored queries. This feature aims to enhance Datasette's utility by enabling the creation of custom interfaces and visualizations for data exploration, with potential for LLM-assisted development.

cards.title: datasette-acl 0.6a0
cards.tldr: Datasette-acl 0.6a0 has been released, expanding its access control capabilities beyond tables to a general resource-sharing system. This update, primarily driven by Alex Garcia, aims to provide multi-user Datasette instances with fine-grained control over resource access. The plugin is being developed to support this broader functionality.

cards.title: GLM-5.2 is probably the most powerful text-only open weights LLM
cards.tldr: Z.ai has released GLM-5.2, a 753B parameter text-only LLM with an MIT license, featuring a 1 million token context window. It now leads independent benchmarks for open-weights models, including the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and ranks second on the Code Arena WebDev leaderboard. However, it is notably token-hungry and its SVG generation capabilities, while impressive for complex scenes like a pelican on a bicycle, have regressed for simpler prompts compared to its predecessor.

cards.title: Quoting Charity Majors
cards.tldr: Charity Majors argues that the economics of code production were fundamentally altered in 2025, making code generation nearly free and instant. This shift has led to code becoming disposable and regenerable, demanding more, not less, engineering discipline.

cards.title: How to write AI agent loops in Claude Code and Codex
cards.tldr: This guide explains how to build AI agent loops using Claude Code and Codex, detailing four loop types: heartbeat, cron, hook, and goal. It emphasizes that loops are essentially automated prompts and outlines five essential components for effective loop design, including work trees, skills, and subagents. The article provides practical examples of building a scheduled PR reviewer in Claude Code and a skills-identification loop in Codex.

cards.title: <click-to-play> — a still that plays
cards.tldr: A new Web Component called "<click-to-play>" has been developed to enhance GIFs on web pages. It displays a static first frame with a play button, only loading the full GIF when the user clicks it. This approach saves bandwidth and improves initial page load times, especially for users who don't intend to watch the GIF.

cards.title: NetNewsWire Status
cards.tldr: Brent Simmons, retired for a year, is dedicating his time to improving NetNewsWire, an open-source RSS reader first released in 2002. He describes it as "like podcasts, but for reading" and has found it indispensable for his own use on Mac and iPhone. This project is free from commercial pressure, allowing for focused development.

cards.title: datasette 1.0a34
cards.tldr: Datasette 1.0a34 introduces tools for inserting, editing, and deleting rows directly within the Datasette web interface. This long-awaited feature was inspired by the addition of SQL write support in Datasette Agent, making it possible to modify data through the chat interface but not the main UI until now.

cards.title: datasette-tailscale 0.1a0
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has released datasette-tailscale 0.1a0, an experimental alpha plugin for Datasette. This plugin allows users to run a Datasette server accessible via Tailscale by using the Tailscale sidecar and Python bindings for the tailscale-rs library. The goal is to make Datasette instances easily accessible on a Tailnet.

cards.title: Quoting Georgi Gerganov
cards.tldr: Georgi Gerganov, known for llama.cpp, has been using the Qwen3.6-27B model daily for coding tasks on his local machines for over a month. He finds it a helpful tool for mundane tasks, despite spending most of his time reviewing pull requests. Gerganov uses a stripped-down version of the pi agent with a custom system prompt for this purpose.

cards.title: The Fable 5 Export Controls Harm US Cyber Defense
cards.tldr: Kate Moussouris argues that the export controls that led to Claude Fable 5 being banned are misguided, as the "jailbreak" involved asking the AI to fix security vulnerabilities. She contends that AI models should be able to identify, fix, and test code for security issues, which is crucial for defensive cybersecurity. Moussouris believes that restricting this capability makes the models less effective at bug fixing and patch verification, potentially harming US cyber defense efforts.

cards.title: Quoting Matteo Wong, The Atlantic
cards.tldr: Cybersecurity expert Katie Moussouris stated that Anthropic shared a White House report on the Fable jailbreak with her for review. The report details how Fable, when prompted to find security issues in insecure code, refused but complied when asked to "fix this code." Moussouris believes this behavior demonstrates the AI model functioning as intended for cybersecurity defense.

cards.title: Cloudflare CAPTCHA on at least one ampersand
cards.tldr: Simon Willison configured Cloudflare's Managed Challenge to only trigger a CAPTCHA for search URLs containing an ampersand, preventing legitimate searches from being blocked. This was achieved by implementing a custom rule that targets URIs starting with "/search/" and containing the "&" character in the query. Willison also experimented with using Claude Code to help generate this rule, though it ultimately interacted with the Cloudflare API.

cards.title: datasette-apps 0.1a2
cards.tldr: Datasette-apps 0.1a2 introduces a new apps-set-csp permission to guard custom network/CSP origins for apps, with an optional allow-list for non-privileged users. The Datasette Agent tool enforces these rules, and the stored query picker now supports keyboard navigation, displaying the three most recent accessible queries. Additionally, fragment links within apps are no longer intercepted by the external-link confirmation modal, and the link confirmation modal and logging panels in full-screen mode have been fixed.

cards.degraded_body: The summary couldn't be generated this week.

cards.title: "They screwed us": Personality clashes sent Anthropic's models offline
cards.tldr: Personality clashes and alleged dismissiveness from Anthropic reportedly led to their AI models being taken offline by the US government. Sources suggest that a lack of perceived safety and security among involved parties, rather than purely technical vulnerabilities, may have been the deciding factor. Anthropic representatives are meeting with the Commerce Department, but the future of their models remains uncertain.

cards.title: Braintrust CEO: Evals are the new PRD for AI products
cards.tldr: Ankur Goyal, CEO of Braintrust, argues that AI evaluations (evals) are becoming the new Product Requirements Document (PRD) for AI products. He highlights how AI agents can now perform tireless, rigorous benchmarking and technical tasks, such as optimizing database queries, which were previously impractical for human engineers. Goyal also introduces the "agent line" framework for determining which tasks can be delegated to AI and discusses encoding subjective qualities like designer taste into repeatable evaluation functions.

cards.title: Quoting Julia Evans
cards.tldr: This week's notable articles include "Datasette Apps" which allows hosting custom HTML applications within Datasette, and "GLM-5.2 is probably the most powerful text-only open weights LLM" highlighting a new powerful open-weights language model. Additionally, there's an article on publishing WASM wheels to PyPI for Pyodide integration.
